name: mob-spawn-group-cap
summary: Raise MobHatchery's spawn-group ceiling from 4096, so every map can run on one zone process.

target.note: Identical in Z:/Server and Z:/ServerSource. Every address below was read out of THIS build.

why: MobHatchery holds its spawn groups as an INLINE FIXED ARRAY, not a pointer: ??0MobHatchery
(0x4B3FC0) runs the eh vector constructor iterator over 0x1000 elements of 0x19B8 bytes, then puts
the List<MobBreederGroup> header at a baked +0x19B8000. That is 25.7MB embedded in the object.
The object is static, not heap: 0x5AD987 stores the CONSTANT 0x13389A48 into the global pointer
?mobhatchery@@3PAVMobHatchery@@A, and a CRT init stub does 'mov ecx,0x13389A48; call ctor'. The
PAV in the symbol is a pointer VARIABLE aimed at a static, which is what makes it look heap-allocated.
It cannot grow in place: the array ends at 0x14D41A48 and ?clockwatch@@3VClockWatch@@A begins at
It CAN be relocated, and that is what this recipe does. All 14 call sites reach the object through
the global pointer; only three instructions carry its raw address. So: append a BSS section with
room, repoint those three immediates at it, and rewrite the two size constants the layout is built
from. No code cave and no allocator call, so there is no new runtime failure mode.
CEILING: 65535. List<MobBreederGroup> is indexed by unsigned short throughout (l_MakeList, l_AllocA,
l_Free all take G). Past that you are retyping the List template, which is a different job.
SIZING: shipped content is 6038 MobRegenGroup records across 88 files (zone 0/1/2/3 = 1628/1962/
1942/261), so one process needs >4096 today, before any 2026 content. 16384 is 2.7x current content
at 103MB -- and one process replaces five, each of which carried its own 25.7MB hatchery inside a
334MB .data image, so consolidating is a large net saving, not a cost.

groups.why: List<MobBreederGroup> handles are unsigned short, and 0xFFFF is the INVALID-HANDLE sentinel the overflow guards test (mh_Load 0x4B6595: cmp ax,0xFFFF). l_MakeList (0x4B3B57) also refuses a capacity of 0xFFFF outright -- it nulls the array and returns an unusable list. So 0xFFFE is the last usable capacity, not 0xFFFF.

new_section.name: .mobhat
new_section.note: Uninitialised: virtual bytes only, zero-filled by the loader, nothing added to the file.
